title: Panna Shines Again As Diamonds Worth Lakhs Bring Luck To A Labourer And A Farmer | India News - News18
text: It is widely known that discovering a diamond in Panna, Madhya Pradesh, is a dream cherished by almost everyone. Although many begin digging with high hopes, most seekers usually return empty-handed. This time, however, the ground has told a different story. Within just 24 hours, two remarkable diamonds have been unearthed, rekindling excitement across the region. On Tuesday, November 9, a valuable 15.34-carat diamond was recovered from the area. Experts believe this precious stone will command a high price at auction. On Wednesday morning, Rajendra Singh from Khajuraho also found his moment of good fortune when he discovered a 3.39-carat gem-quality diamond. According to initial estimates, the stone is worth around Rs 10 to 12 lakh. Rajendra Singh shared that he has deposited the diamond at the office, from where it will be sent for auction. He recounted that a few years ago he had suffered a heart attack and last year he was paralysed, leaving him unable to continue farming. He later came to Panna, offered prayers at the feet of Jugalkishore Sarkar, and resolved to try his hand at diamond mining. Seven months ago, he took a lease in Krishnakalyanpur Patti and began excavation work with labourers. His perseverance has finally borne fruit. He added that the auction money will be used to provide his two children with better education, while he himself intends to continue working in the mine. Diamond expert Anupam Singh confirmed that the 3.39-carat stone is of gem quality and will soon go under the hammer, where it is expected to fetch an excellent price. Another story of hope and perseverance has emerged from Madhya Pradesh’s gemstone city, Panna, which has once again displayed its generosity. Satish, a 28-year-old labourer from Raniganj Mohalla, has seen his fortunes transform after unearthing a 15.34-carat gem-quality diamond from a shallow mine in Krishna Kalyanpur. Diamond experts estimate its value to be around Rs 70 to 80 lakh, a life-changing sum for his family, who had long been struggling with poverty. Satish had taken the mine on lease from November 14 to December 31, 2025. For 20 days, he and his family sifted tirelessly through dust and gravel until, at last, a stroke of extraordinary luck appeared. After discovering the diamond, Satish deposited it at the district diamond office. Once the stone is sold at the upcoming auction, the remaining amount, after the deduction of government taxes, will be transferred to his account. Reflecting on his situation, Satish said that his family’s financial condition had been so dire that even securing two meals a day was difficult on daily wages. With the proceeds from the auction, he hopes to marry off his two sisters, support his family, and start a small business. Diamond expert Anupam Singh confirmed that the stone is of excellent gem quality and is expected to attract strong bids at auction, remarking that the Panna mines are known for such remarkable turns of fortune. These mines, famous across the country, offer even small landholders and labourers the hope of striking it rich. While the district administration congratulated Satish, experts also issued a reminder against illegal mining. Satish and Rajendra’s discovery stands as inspiring examples that perseverance rarely goes unrewarded.
